## Overview

Use InstantTensor 0.2.2's pre-I/O tensor filter for models that identify unused checkpoint weights, including supported MTP draft models.

Related: [scitix/InstantTensor#14](https://github.com/scitix/InstantTensor/issues/14), implemented upstream by [scitix/InstantTensor#29](https://github.com/scitix/InstantTensor/pull/29).

## Claims

### Problem

MTP speculative decoding loads a small draft model from the target model's checkpoint. vLLM can already omit checkpoint files containing only unused weights, but retained files can mix required draft weights with unused target weights. InstantTensor previously read every tensor in those retained files.

### Solution

Read tensor names from the safetensors headers and apply the model's existing `is_unused_checkpoint_weight` predicate. Pass the selected names to InstantTensor using exact matching, before native payload I/O starts.

### Benefits

- Unused tensors in mixed checkpoint files no longer need to be streamed.
- InstantTensor's progress total and buffer sizing describe the selected tensors.
- The existing model-specific rules retain shared embeddings and output heads where needed.

This is a selective-I/O feature, not a measured startup-speed claim. Aligned reads can include neighboring bytes.

## Validation

### Verification

Passed locally on Python 3.12.3 / Torch 2.13.0:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_filter_duplicate_safetensors.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/instanttensor_loader/test_weight_utils.py -v
```

Result: **13 passed, 4 skipped**. The four skips require CUDA. The CPU tests use real safetensors files and substitute the native InstantTensor boundary; they cover partial, all, empty, and absent selection, source prefixes, shared weights, exact-name matching arguments, and process-group selection.

Also passed: Ruff 0.14.0 check/format, isolated repository mypy hook (Python 3.11 target), typos, markdownlint-cli2 0.21.0, `git diff --check`, `uv pip check`, and the applicable local pre-commit hooks, including test-to-CI tethering.

The complete pre-commit environment could not initialize because one hook's public Git repository was unavailable. Equivalent available linters and the unchanged local hooks were run directly. ROCm lock regeneration was verified. Exact CUDA/CPU lock regeneration was blocked by the unavailable PyTorch download index; those locks contain only the matching InstantTensor version update, without unrelated dependency changes.

Native CUDA loading, multi-GPU MTP generation, and before/after startup benchmarks require GPU validation before submission. In particular, compare identical checkpoints, InstantTensor versions, storage settings, TP/PP settings, and cache conditions; record draft-load time, selected bytes, total startup time, and generation correctness. Confirm that speculative decoding actually accepts draft tokens.

The added tests live under `tests/model_executor`, which is collected by the existing Model Executor Buildkite job.

## Details

### Changes

- Forward the source's unused-weight predicate to the InstantTensor iterator.
- Build an exact allowlist from checkpoint metadata, before source-prefix application or model-specific name mapping.
- Use independent per-GPU reads for sources with a predicate. InstantTensor 0.2.2 rejects filtering with any NCCL process group. Even a predicate that keeps every tensor uses this mode, so filtered loads do not depend on participation by other ranks.
- Return without opening the native loader when the predicate selects no tensors.
- Preserve coordinated distributed loading when no predicate exists, and keep `copy=True` so yielded tensors retain ownership of their storage.
- Require InstantTensor 0.2.2 and update its test requirements.

Independent reads lose InstantTensor's cooperative multi-GPU I/O, so the tradeoff depends on checkpoint layout and storage. This does not implement general pipeline-stage selection, tensor-parallel slicing, or new selection rules for models without the existing hook.

### Diff size

Against base `12b005eefa06f97eeebfae3e14bcac5fa3b81197`:

| Category | Added | Removed | Net |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Documentation | 17 | 1 | +16 |
| Configuration | 4 | 4 | 0 |
| Runtime | 37 | 8 | +29 |
| Tests | 117 | 2 | +115 |
| Generated test requirements | 4 | 4 | 0 |
| **Total** | **179** | **19** | **+160** |

Configuration includes `setup.py`, `requirements/cuda.txt`, and the CUDA/ROCm test inputs. Generated test requirements are the CUDA/CPU/ROCm locks and the nightly-torch file. Each changed file is counted once.

+## Selective loading
+
+For models that provide `is_unused_checkpoint_weight`, including supported MTP
+draft models, vLLM passes the required checkpoint tensor names to InstantTensor.
+Unused tensors are skipped before payload I/O, including those in shards that also
+contain required weights. Names are matched exactly, before vLLM applies any source
+prefix or model-specific name mapping. Progress and buffer sizing reflect only the
+selected tensors; reads can still include neighboring bytes for alignment.
+
+InstantTensor 0.2.2 requires filtered loads to read independently on each GPU,
+without an NCCL process group. A filtered load therefore trades coordinated
+multi-GPU I/O for reading fewer tensors; the performance benefit depends on the
+checkpoint layout and storage. Without this hook, dense and fused-expert
+checkpoints retain coordinated distributed loading; expert-parallel filtering of
+individually indexed expert weights uses independent reads. When both filters
+apply, only tensors selected by both are read. This does not automatically select
+pipeline-stage weights or tensor-parallel slices.
+
 ## Benchmarks
